title: NRC Reviews of Reactor Designs Previously Authorized by U.S. Department of Energy or Department of War (final rule)
date_evidence: Federal Register / Vol. 91, No. 205 / Monday, October 26, 2026 / Rules and Regulations
key_claim: The final rule lets commercial applicants use information from DOE or Department of War authorised reactors that have been tested, but applicants must show how the authorisation satisfies NRC regulations and close any gaps; nothing delegates NRC functions, and the NRC could not quantify the savings.
frame_summary: The NRC frames the rule as an optional evidentiary pathway that keeps its independent review and safety standard intact while avoiding repeat technical reviews where scopes match.
verbatim_quote: In response to the proposed rule, the NRC received 136 unique comment submissions.
verbatim_list: This final rule is effective on November 25, 2026.
The NRC was not able to quantify these potential savings in a useful way at this time.
Nothing in this rule delegates to DOE, DOW, or any other agency
not all prior DOE or DOW authorizations may meet the full scope of requirements

title: Shared Data, Independent Review
key_claim: DOE and DOW information should receive no presumption of sufficiency or regulatory credit based solely on its source, and the rule should be a narrow evidentiary clarification, not an expedited approval track.
frame_summary: Argues for NRC and DOE data sharing that stops short of letting prior federal authorisation substitute for NRC safety findings.
verbatim_quote: receives no presumption of sufficiency, evidentiary preference, or regulatory credit based solely on its source
verbatim_list: not a new expedited approval track or a transfer of licensing authority

title: NRC Finalizes Rule Allowing Reactor Applicants to Use DOE, DOW Demonstration Data
key_claim: Four DOE-authorised reactors reached zero-power fueled criticality by July 4, 2026 and a fifth on August 5; such demonstrations do not show sustained electricity production or complete plant performance.

title: NRC Finalizes DOE-to-NRC Licensing Pathway Rulemaking: The Regulatory Crosswalk Takes Shape
key_claim: The NRC declined to presume DOE or DOW findings acceptable; credit is set application by application, limited-duration demonstrations may not establish material suitability, the NRC does not oversee construction under DOE authorisation, and fuel cycle facilities are outside the rule.
frame_summary: A law firm explains the rule as a crosswalk whose credit is decided case by case, with specific evidence gaps the NRC staff expects to remain.

title: NRC Finalizes Pathway for Reactor Designs Previously Authorized by DOE or DOW
